newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU plans to cut artists in on sales.
newsitem.headline: EU plans to cut artists in on sales.

text.p: The European Parliament backed on Wednesday European Union plans to ensure artists throughout the 15-nation bloc receive a slice of the price whenever their works are resold.
But artists representatives said it was a mixed blessing.
As things stand some EU countries, notably Britain, do not recognise a "resale right" and so, unlike writers, artists feel none of the benefit when their paintings are resold.

Under the European Commission's proposal artists throughout the bloc would be entitled to the same level of royalty, set on a sliding scale according to the selling price of their painting, sculpture or artefact.

Spanish conservative deputy Ana Palacio Vallelersundi, who reported on ther proposal for the EU assembly, told Reuters she had tried to find a balance between the concerns of major auction houses like Sothebys and Christies and the artists whose works they sell.
Sotheby's and Christies say they fear that once the resale right is enforced in Britain it will force the art market to move from London to New York and Switzerland.

Artists' organisations say on the other hand that artists in countries like France and Germany could get less money than they do now as the parliament wanted to cut the percentages proposed by the EU executive.
The authors' organisation GESAC said that under the Parliament proposal a French artist, currently entitled to three percent of a 250,000-ecu ($280,000) sale, would get 23 percent less.
In Germany, where the artist's cut is five percent, the loss would be 54 percent, it said.
But Palaceo said that in exchange the French and German artists would for the first time be paid when their paintings were resold on the major London art market.
